     request: Request,
"""S20: "I've paid". A customer who paid in her own UPI app tells the shop, on the thank-you / status page.

This is a CLAIM and is always worded as one ("says paid"). LaunchWitness never sees a bank, never checks a payment and
never calls an order paid: the owner looks in her own UPI app and marks the order Paid herself (the existing status flow).

What is kept: the 12-digit UPI reference (UTR) and, optionally, ONE screenshot, re-encoded from its pixels as WebP by the
same gate as shop photos (size cap, content sniff, pixel cap, no metadata). Both are private to the owner: never in an
audit row, evidence, the shared report, a log or a public page. They go with the order, the shop or the account, and
30 days after the order is Done or Cancelled (`purge_old`, run by the daily job).
"""

import io
import re
from datetime import timedelta

from PIL import Image
from sqlmodel import Session, delete, func, select

from app import audit, photos
from app.config import Settings
from app.mail.smtp import Mailer
from app.models import Business, Order, PaymentClaim, utcnow
from app.sites.render import format_inr

MAX_SHOT_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024  # a phone screenshot is well under this; the body is refused above it
MAX_BODY_BYTES = MAX_SHOT_BYTES + 64 * 1024  # the whole form
SHOT_WIDTH = 900  # wide enough to read a UPI receipt
KEEP_DAYS = 30  # after the order is Done or Cancelled
SUBMITS_PER_ORDER = 6  # one claim per order; a few corrections allowed
CLAIMS_PER_VISITOR_PER_HOUR = 10
UTR = re.compile(r"^[0-9]{12}$")  # ASCII digits only (\d would accept Arabic-Indic and other Unicode digits)


class ClaimRefused(ValueError):
    """Plain words for the customer."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, status: int = 422):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status


def parse_utr(text: str) -> str:
    """Exactly 12 digits; spaces (and dashes people copy along) are accepted and dropped."""
    digits = re.sub(r"[\s\-]", "", text or "")
    if not UTR.match(digits):
        raise ClaimRefused("Please enter the 12-digit UPI reference number (UTR) from your payment, for example "
                           "4021 5678 9012. You can find it in your UPI app under the payment.")
    return digits


def show_utr(utr: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(utr[i:i + 4] for i in range(0, len(utr), 4))


def process_screenshot(data: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, int, int]:
    """Same gate as shop photos (photos.clean_image), one WebP at SHOT_WIDTH. Nothing of the original survives."""
    try:
        clean = photos.clean_image(data, max_bytes=MAX_SHOT_BYTES)
    except photos.PhotoRefused as e:
        raise ClaimRefused(str(e).replace("photo", "screenshot")) from None
    if clean.width > SHOT_WIDTH:
        clean = clean.resize((SHOT_WIDTH, round(clean.height * SHOT_WIDTH / clean.width)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    out = io.BytesIO()
    clean.save(out, "WEBP", quality=photos.QUALITY, method=4)  # no exif=, no icc_profile=
    return out.getvalue(), clean.width, clean.height


def order_for_token(session: Session, business: Business, token: str) -> Order | None:
    """The real order behind a status link: this shop's, never a test order, and only for a well-formed token."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,64}", token or ""):
        return None
    return session.exec(select(Order).where(Order.business_id == business.id, Order.status_token == token,
                                            Order.is_test == False)).first()  # noqa: E712


def claim_for(session: Session, order_id: int | None) -> PaymentClaim | None:
    if order_id is None:
        return None
    return session.exec(select(PaymentClaim).where(PaymentClaim.order_id == order_id)).first()


def submit(session: Session, settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, *, business: Business, profile, order: Order,
           utr_text: str, screenshot: bytes | None, visitor: str, channel: str = "smtp") -> PaymentClaim:
    """Store (or replace) the order's claim and tell the owner once. Raises ClaimRefused."""
    if order.is_test:
        raise ClaimRefused("This is a test order.", 404)
    if order.status in ("done", "cancelled"):
        raise ClaimRefused("This order is already closed. Please message the shop if you have a question.", 409)
    if not order.pay_now_inr:
        raise ClaimRefused("There is nothing to pay now for this order.", 409)
    now = utcnow()
    mine = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(PaymentClaim).where(
        PaymentClaim.visitor == visitor, PaymentClaim.updated_at >= now - timedelta(hours=1))).one()
    row = claim_for(session, order.id)
    if (row is not None and row.submits >= SUBMITS_PER_ORDER) or (mine >= CLAIMS_PER_VISITOR_PER_HOUR and visitor):
        audit.record(session, actor="customer", action="payment_claim", target=f"order:{order.id}", result="blocked",
                     business_id=business.id, detail="rate limit")
        raise ClaimRefused("You have sent this a few times already. Please message the shop on WhatsApp instead.", 429)
    utr = parse_utr(utr_text)  # after the rate limit: a bad guess still counts as nothing, but never stores anything
    shot = process_screenshot(screenshot) if screenshot else None
    replaced = row is not None
    if row is None:
        row = PaymentClaim(business_id=business.id, order_id=order.id, utr=utr, visitor=visitor)
    else:
        row.utr, row.visitor, row.submits, row.updated_at = utr, visitor, row.submits + 1, now
    row.screenshot, row.screenshot_w, row.screenshot_h = (shot[0], shot[1], shot[2]) if shot else (None, 0, 0)
    session.add(row)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(row)
    # Audited WITHOUT the UTR or the image: only that a claim came, whether it replaced one, and whether it has a picture.
    audit.record(session, actor="customer", action="payment_claim", target=f"order:{order.id}", result="ok",
                 business_id=business.id,
                 detail=("replaced an earlier claim" if replaced else "customer says paid") + (", with a screenshot" if shot else ""))
    if not replaced:
        notify_owner(session, settings, mailer, business=business, profile=profile, order=order, claim=row, channel=channel)
    return row


def notify_owner(session: Session, settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, *, business: Business, profile, order: Order,
                 claim: PaymentClaim, channel: str = "smtp") -> None:
    """One email: "Riya says she paid ₹650 for LW-XXXX (UTR ...). Check your UPI app, then mark it Paid." Never for a test order."""
    from app import outbox
    from app.sites.orders import order_recipients

    first = order.customer_name.split()[0] if order.customer_name.split() else "Your customer"
    orders_url = f"{settings.app_base_url.rstrip('/')}/#/b/{business.id}/orders"
    amount = format_inr(order.pay_now_inr)
    subject = f"{first} says they paid {amount} for {order.ref}"
    body = "\n".join([
        f"{order.customer_name} says they paid {amount} for {order.ref} (UTR {show_utr(claim.utr)}).",
        "",
        "This is what the customer told us. LaunchWitness does not see your bank and cannot check it.",
        "Check your UPI app. If the money is there, mark the order Paid:",
        orders_url,
        "",
        "If you can't find it, message the customer (their WhatsApp is on the order) before you send anything."])
    outbox.send(session, settings, mailer, kind="payment_claim", key=f"payclaim:{order.id}",
                to=", ".join(order_recipients(session, settings, business)), subject=subject, body=body, channel=channel,
                business_id=business.id,  # no order_id: the order's own "email sent" status stays about the order email
                ref={"audit": {"actor": "system", "action": "payment_claim_email", "target": f"order:{order.id}"}})


def purge_old(session: Session, now=None) -> int:
    """Claims (UTR + screenshot) of orders that were Done or Cancelled more than KEEP_DAYS ago. Run by the daily job."""
    cutoff = (now or utcnow()) - timedelta(days=KEEP_DAYS)
    ids = session.exec(select(Order.id).where(Order.status.in_(("done", "cancelled")),  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                                              Order.status_changed_at < cutoff)).all()
    if not ids:
        return 0
    n = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(PaymentClaim).where(
        PaymentClaim.order_id.in_(ids))).one()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    if n:
        session.exec(delete(PaymentClaim).where(PaymentClaim.order_id.in_(ids)))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        session.commit()
        audit.record(session, actor="system", action="payment_claims_purged", result="ok",
                     detail=f"{n} payment note(s) removed, 30 days after the order closed")
    return n


def purge_job(engine) -> int:
    """The daily job (and once at start-up): opens its own session, never raises into the scheduler."""
    try:
        with Session(engine) as s:
            return purge_old(s)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  a failed purge is retried tomorrow; it must never stop the scheduler
        return 0

"""S20: "I've paid". A customer who paid in her own UPI app tells the shop, on the thank-you / status page.

This is a CLAIM and is always worded as one ("says paid"). LaunchWitness never sees a bank, never checks a payment and
never calls an order paid: the owner looks in her own UPI app and marks the order Paid herself (the existing status flow).

What is kept: the 12-digit UPI reference (UTR) and, optionally, ONE screenshot, re-encoded from its pixels as WebP by the
same gate as shop photos (size cap, content sniff, pixel cap, no metadata). Both are private to the owner: never in an
audit row, evidence, the shared report, a log or a public page. They go with the order, the shop or the account, and
30 days after the order is Done or Cancelled (`purge_old`, run by the daily job).
"""

import io
import re
from datetime import timedelta

from PIL import Image
from sqlmodel import Session, delete, func, select

from app import audit, photos
from app.config import Settings
from app.mail.smtp import Mailer
from app.models import Business, Order, PaymentClaim, utcnow
from app.sites.render import format_inr

MAX_SHOT_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024  # a phone screenshot is well under this; the body is refused above it
MAX_BODY_BYTES = MAX_SHOT_BYTES + 64 * 1024  # the whole form
SHOT_WIDTH = 900  # wide enough to read a UPI receipt
KEEP_DAYS = 30  # after the order is Done or Cancelled
SUBMITS_PER_ORDER = 6  # one claim per order; a few corrections allowed
CLAIMS_PER_VISITOR_PER_HOUR = 10
UTR = re.compile(r"^[0-9]{12}$")  # ASCII digits only (\d would accept Arabic-Indic and other Unicode digits)


class ClaimRefused(ValueError):
    """Plain words for the customer."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, status: int = 422):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.status = status


def parse_utr(text: str) -> str:
    """Exactly 12 digits; spaces (and dashes people copy along) are accepted and dropped."""
    digits = re.sub(r"[\s\-]", "", text or "")
    if not UTR.match(digits):
        raise ClaimRefused("Please enter the 12-digit UPI reference number (UTR) from your payment, for example "
                           "4021 5678 9012. You can find it in your UPI app under the payment.")
    return digits


def show_utr(utr: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(utr[i:i + 4] for i in range(0, len(utr), 4))


def process_screenshot(data: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, int, int]:
    """Same gate as shop photos (photos.clean_image), one WebP at SHOT_WIDTH. Nothing of the original survives."""
    try:
        clean = photos.clean_image(data, max_bytes=MAX_SHOT_BYTES)
    except photos.PhotoRefused as e:
        raise ClaimRefused(str(e).replace("photo", "screenshot")) from None
    if clean.width > SHOT_WIDTH:
        clean = clean.resize((SHOT_WIDTH, round(clean.height * SHOT_WIDTH / clean.width)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    out = io.BytesIO()
    clean.save(out, "WEBP", quality=photos.QUALITY, method=4)  # no exif=, no icc_profile=
    return out.getvalue(), clean.width, clean.height


def order_for_token(session: Session, business: Business, token: str) -> Order | None:
    """The real order behind a status link: this shop's, never a test order, and only for a well-formed token."""
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,64}", token or ""):
        return None
    return session.exec(select(Order).where(Order.business_id == business.id, Order.status_token == token,
                                            Order.is_test == False)).first()  # noqa: E712


def claim_for(session: Session, order_id: int | None) -> PaymentClaim | None:
    if order_id is None:
        return None
    return session.exec(select(PaymentClaim).where(PaymentClaim.order_id == order_id)).first()


def submit(session: Session, settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, *, business: Business, profile, order: Order,
           utr_text: str, screenshot: bytes | None, visitor: str, channel: str = "smtp") -> PaymentClaim:
    """Store (or replace) the order's claim and tell the owner once. Raises ClaimRefused."""
    if order.is_test:
        raise ClaimRefused("This is a test order.", 404)
    if order.status in ("done", "cancelled"):
        raise ClaimRefused("This order is already closed. Please message the shop if you have a question.", 409)
    if not order.pay_now_inr:
        raise ClaimRefused("There is nothing to pay now for this order.", 409)
    now = utcnow()
    mine = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(PaymentClaim).where(
        PaymentClaim.visitor == visitor, PaymentClaim.updated_at >= now - timedelta(hours=1))).one()
    row = claim_for(session, order.id)
    if (row is not None and row.submits >= SUBMITS_PER_ORDER) or (mine >= CLAIMS_PER_VISITOR_PER_HOUR and visitor):
        audit.record(session, actor="customer", action="payment_claim", target=f"order:{order.id}", result="blocked",
                     business_id=business.id, detail="rate limit")
        raise ClaimRefused("You have sent this a few times already. Please message the shop on WhatsApp instead.", 429)
    utr = parse_utr(utr_text)  # after the rate limit: a bad guess still counts as nothing, but never stores anything
    shot = process_screenshot(screenshot) if screenshot else None
    replaced = row is not None
    if row is None:
        row = PaymentClaim(business_id=business.id, order_id=order.id, utr=utr, visitor=visitor)
    else:
        row.utr, row.visitor, row.submits, row.updated_at = utr, visitor, row.submits + 1, now
    row.screenshot, row.screenshot_w, row.screenshot_h = (shot[0], shot[1], shot[2]) if shot else (None, 0, 0)
    session.add(row)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(row)
    # Audited WITHOUT the UTR or the image: only that a claim came, whether it replaced one, and whether it has a picture.
    audit.record(session, actor="customer", action="payment_claim", target=f"order:{order.id}", result="ok",
                 business_id=business.id,
                 detail=("replaced an earlier claim" if replaced else "customer says paid") + (", with a screenshot" if shot else ""))
    if not replaced:
        notify_owner(session, settings, mailer, business=business, profile=profile, order=order, claim=row, channel=channel)
    return row


def notify_owner(session: Session, settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, *, business: Business, profile, order: Order,
                 claim: PaymentClaim, channel: str = "smtp") -> None:
    """One email: "Riya says she paid ₹650 for LW-XXXX (UTR ...). Check your UPI app, then mark it Paid." Never for a test order."""
    from app import outbox
    from app.sites.orders import order_recipients

    first = order.customer_name.split()[0] if order.customer_name.split() else "Your customer"
    orders_url = f"{settings.app_base_url.rstrip('/')}/#/b/{business.id}/orders"
    amount = format_inr(order.pay_now_inr)
    subject = f"{first} says they paid {amount} for {order.ref}"
    body = "\n".join([
        f"{order.customer_name} says they paid {amount} for {order.ref} (UTR {show_utr(claim.utr)}).",
        "",
        "This is what the customer told us. LaunchWitness does not see your bank and cannot check it.",
        "Check your UPI app. If the money is there, mark the order Paid:",
        orders_url,
        "",
        "If you can't find it, message the customer (their WhatsApp is on the order) before you send anything."])
    outbox.send(session, settings, mailer, kind="payment_claim", key=f"payclaim:{order.id}",
                to=", ".join(order_recipients(session, settings, business)), subject=subject, body=body, channel=channel,
                business_id=business.id,  # no order_id: the order's own "email sent" status stays about the order email
                ref={"audit": {"actor": "system", "action": "payment_claim_email", "target": f"order:{order.id}"}})


def purge_old(session: Session, now=None) -> int:
    """Claims (UTR + screenshot) of orders that were Done or Cancelled more than KEEP_DAYS ago. Run by the daily job."""
    cutoff = (now or utcnow()) - timedelta(days=KEEP_DAYS)
    ids = session.exec(select(Order.id).where(Order.status.in_(("done", "cancelled")),  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
                                              Order.status_changed_at < cutoff)).all()
    if not ids:
        return 0
    n = session.exec(select(func.count()).select_from(PaymentClaim).where(
        PaymentClaim.order_id.in_(ids))).one()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    if n:
        session.exec(delete(PaymentClaim).where(PaymentClaim.order_id.in_(ids)))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        session.commit()
        audit.record(session, actor="system", action="payment_claims_purged", result="ok",
                     detail=f"{n} payment note(s) removed, 30 days after the order closed")
    return n


def purge_job(engine) -> int:
    """The daily job (and once at start-up): opens its own session, never raises into the scheduler."""
    try:
        with Session(engine) as s:
            return purge_old(s)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  a failed purge is retried tomorrow; it must never stop the scheduler
        return 0

def edit(client, biz: dict, **changes) -> dict:
    cur = client.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}").json()
    r = client.put(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}", json={"profile": {**cur["profile"], **changes}, "subdomain": cur["subdomain"]})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.json()


def shop(client) -> str:
    r = client.get("/", headers=HOST)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    return r.text


def order_page(client) -> str:
    r = client.post("/order", data=ORDER, headers=HOST)
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.text


def wa(html: str, number: str) -> bool:
    return f"wa.me/91{number}" in html


def test_changed_upi_stays_old_for_customers_until_she_confirms(client, engine):
    biz = live_shop(client, engine)
    assert OLD_UPI not in shop(client)  # S20: the shop page never carries the UPI ID
    edit(client, biz, payment_terms="upfront")  # so the thank-you page carries a UPI link for the full amount
    out = edit(client, biz, upi_id=NEW_UPI, upi_display_name="Someone Else")
    assert out["status"] == "live" and out["public"] is True  # still live
    assert out["confirm_new"] == ["upi"]
    page, thanks = shop(client), order_page(client)
    for html in (page, thanks):
        assert NEW_UPI not in html and "Someone Else" not in html
    assert f"upi://pay?pa={OLD_UPI}" in thanks.replace("&", "&")  # the payment link carries the confirmed ID
    # she sees her own new value (Review), only customers get the confirmed one
    assert out["profile"]["upi_id"] == NEW_UPI
    assert client.post(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}/confirm", json={"what": "upi"}).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}").json()["confirm_new"] == []
    assert NEW_UPI not in shop(client) and f"upi://pay?pa={NEW_UPI}" in order_page(client).replace("&", "&")


def test_changed_whatsapp_stays_old_until_confirmed(client, engine):
    biz = live_shop(client, engine)
    out = edit(client, biz, whatsapp=NEW_WA)
    assert out["confirm_new"] == ["whatsapp"]
    page = shop(client)
    assert not wa(page, "9123456789") and wa(page, OLD_WA_DIGITS)
    assert client.post(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}/confirm", json={"what": "whatsapp"}).status_code == 200
    assert wa(shop(client), "9123456789")


def test_both_changed_twice_keeps_the_first_confirmed_values(client, engine):
    biz = live_shop(client, engine)
    edit(client, biz, upi_id=NEW_UPI, whatsapp=NEW_WA)
    out = edit(client, biz, upi_id="third.one@okicici", whatsapp="99999 11111")
    assert out["confirm_new"] == ["upi", "whatsapp"]
    page = shop(client)
    assert "third.one" not in page and NEW_UPI not in page and OLD_UPI not in page  # S20: not on the shop page at all

TOKEN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$")


def existing_order(session: Session, business: Business, token: str) -> Order | None:
    """The order already made with this form token (a double tap or a re-sent form), if any."""
    if not TOKEN.match(token):
        return None
    return session.exec(select(Order).where(Order.business_id == business.id, Order.client_token == token)).first()


def order_view(order: Order, claim=None) -> dict:
    """What the thank-you / status page may show. Deliberately NOT the street address: that stays with the owner.
    S20: `status_url` (a real order's own unguessable page), the shop's own update, and only the LAST 4 digits of a claim."""
    return {"is_test": order.is_test, "status_url": f"/order/{order.status_token}" if order.status_token else "",
            "status_label": STATUS_LABELS.get(order.status, "") if order.status_token else "", "status": order.status,
            "claim": {"last4": claim.utr[-4:], "has_shot": bool(claim.screenshot)} if claim is not None else None,
            "customer_name": order.customer_name, "customer_phone": order.customer_phone, "note": order.note,
            "items": json.loads(order.items_json), "total_inr": order.total_inr, "ref": order.ref,
            "fulfilment": order.fulfilment, "delivery_pin": order.delivery_pin, "wanted_date": order.wanted_date,
            "time_slot": order.time_slot, "fee_inr": order.fee_inr, "payment_terms": order.payment_terms,
            "pay_now_inr": order.pay_now_inr, "pay_later_inr": order.pay_later_inr}


def place_order(session: Session, mailer: Mailer, settings: Settings, *, business: Business, profile: Profile,
                data: dict, is_test: bool = False, nonce: str = "", visitor: str = "", token: str = "",
                confirm_url: str = "", channel: str = "smtp", recipients: list[str] | None = None) -> Order:
    """Store the order, then email it to `order_recipients` through the outbox. The launch check's test order and
    a customer's order both come through here, so a passing test order proves the real path.

    S13: the order is saved first and its email queued; the outbox tries it at once and keeps retrying if the
    mail server is slow or down, so a customer's order is never lost. `email_status` follows the outbox row."""
    from app import outbox

    order = Order(business_id=business.id, customer_name=data["customer_name"], customer_phone=data["customer_phone"],
                  items_json=json.dumps(data["items"], ensure_ascii=False), total_inr=data["total_inr"],
                  note=data["note"], is_test=is_test, nonce=nonce, visitor=visitor, ref=new_ref(),
                  client_token=token if TOKEN.match(token) else "", email_status="queued",
                  status_token="" if is_test else secrets.token_urlsafe(24),
                  fulfilment=data.get("fulfilment", ""), delivery_address=data.get("delivery_address", ""),
                  delivery_pin=data.get("delivery_pin", ""), wanted_date=data.get("wanted_date", ""),
                  time_slot=data.get("time_slot", ""), fee_inr=data.get("fee_inr", 0),
                  payment_terms=data.get("payment_terms", ""), pay_now_inr=data.get("pay_now_inr", 0),
                  pay_later_inr=data.get("pay_later_inr", 0))
    session.add(order)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(order)
    audit.record(session, actor="checker" if is_test else "customer", action="order_placed", target=f"order:{order.id}", result="ok",
                 business_id=business.id,  # never the address, PIN or phone: only counts and the mode
                 detail=f"{len(data['items'])} item(s), total {data['total_inr']}"
                 + (f", {data['fulfilment']}" if data.get("fulfilment") else ""))

    recipients = recipients or order_recipients(session, settings, business)
    orders_url = f"{settings.app_base_url.rstrip('/')}/#/b/{business.id}/orders"
    subject, body = order_email(business, profile, order, data["items"], confirm_url, orders_url)
    kind = "test_order" if is_test else "order"
    outbox.send(session, settings, mailer, kind=kind, key=f"order:{order.id}", to=", ".join(recipients),
                subject=subject, body=body, channel=channel, business_id=business.id, order_id=order.id,
                # a test order that can't go out soon is useless (the next check sends a new one)
                expires_at=utcnow() + timedelta(minutes=30) if is_test else None,
                ref={"audit": {"actor": "system", "action": "order_email", "target": f"order:{order.id}"}})
    session.refresh(order)
    return order


def accept_order_form(session: Session, settings: Settings, mailer: Mailer, *, business: Business, profile: Profile,
                      form: dict[str, str], visitor: str, channel: str = "smtp") -> tuple[int, str]:
    """What the shop's order form does with a POST: (HTTP status, page HTML). The public route and the
    checker's practice test order both come through here, so the test order exercises the real path.

    A POST carrying `lw_test=<nonce>` of an OPEN test ticket for this shop becomes a hidden test order
    (not counted in limits, not in the seller's list). Any other value is ignored."""
    from app import payclaims, proof
    from app.sites.render import render_site

    token = form.get("order_token", "")
    again = existing_order(session, business, token)
    if again is not None:  # double tap / form sent twice: show the same thank-you, make nothing new
        return 200, render_site(profile, page="thanks", order=order_view(again, payclaims.claim_for(session, again.id)))
    ticket = proof.open_ticket(session, business, form.get("lw_test", ""))  # the checker's own test order, or None
    shown = {"session": session, "business": business}
    if ticket is None and ful.on_break(profile):  # S15: refused politely here, not only in the page; the checker's test order is not
        audit.record(session, actor="customer", action="order_placed", target=f"business:{business.id}", result="blocked",
                     business_id=business.id, detail="shop is taking a break")
        return 409, render_site(profile, form_error=ful.break_refusal(profile), form_values=form,
                                full_dates=full_days(session, business, profile))
    try:
        data = parse_order_form(form, profile, test=ticket is not None, session=session, business=business)
    except OrderInvalid as e:
        return 422, render_site(profile, form_error=str(e), form_values=form, full_dates=full_days(**shown, profile=profile))
    if ticket is None:
        try:
            check_order_limits(session, settings, business, visitor)
        except TooManyOrders:
            return 429, render_site(profile, form_error=TOO_MANY, form_values=form,
                                    full_dates=full_days(**shown, profile=profile))
        order = place_order(session, mailer, settings, business=business, profile=profile, data=data, visitor=visitor,
                            token=token, channel=channel)
    else:
        # S19B: a monitoring test goes to our check mailbox and has no "Yes, I got it" link (a tap there would
        # claim her inbox got it when it didn't)
        confirm_url = "" if ticket.audience == "check" else proof.issue_confirm_link(session, settings, ticket)
        order = place_order(session, mailer, settings, business=business, profile=profile, data=data, is_test=True,
                            nonce=ticket.nonce, visitor="", token=token, confirm_url=confirm_url, channel=channel,
                            recipients=test_recipients(session, settings, business, ticket.audience))
        proof.ticket_used(session, ticket, order)
    return 200, render_site(profile, page="thanks", order=order_view(order))

"""Session 20B: fixes to S20 Part A before it goes live.

- the status link's token is stored only as its SHA-256 (like every other token);
- the thank-you / status page greets the customer by first name only;
- pay-on-delivery orders never get UPI details or the "I've paid" form;
- shop hosts answer /favicon.ico with 204 (the app host keeps its own).
"""

import hashlib

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app.models import Order
from tests.test_s20_payments import HOST, ORDER, claim, live_shop, place


def real_order(engine) -> Order:
    with Session(engine) as s:
        return s.exec(select(Order).where(Order.is_test == False)).first()  # noqa: E712


# ---------- 1. the status token is stored hashed ----------

def test_status_token_is_stored_only_as_its_sha256(client, engine):
    live_shop(client, engine)
    html, tok = place(client)
    o = real_order(engine)
    assert o.status_token == hashlib.sha256(tok.encode()).hexdigest()
    assert tok not in o.status_token and tok not in o.model_dump_json()  # the raw token is nowhere in the row
    page = client.get(f"/order/{tok}", headers=HOST)
    assert page.status_code == 200 and f'href="/order/{tok}"' in page.text  # the link on the page is the raw one
    # the stored hash is not itself a key to the page
    assert client.get(f"/order/{o.status_token}", headers=HOST).status_code == 404
    assert claim(client, o.status_token).status_code == 404
    assert claim(client, tok).status_code == 303


def test_a_resent_form_issues_a_fresh_link_and_the_old_one_stops(client, engine):
    live_shop(client, engine)
    form = {**ORDER, "order_token": "resend-token-0123456789"}
    _, first = place(client, **form)
    _, second = place(client, **form)  # the same form sent again: no new order, a fresh link
    with Session(engine) as s:
        assert len(s.exec(select(Order).where(Order.is_test == False)).all()) == 1  # noqa: E712
    assert first != second
    assert client.get(f"/order/{second}", headers=HOST).status_code == 200
    assert client.get(f"/order/{first}", headers=HOST).status_code == 404

"""Session 19D (Part 7a): customers only ever see a live shop's last CONFIRMED WhatsApp number and UPI ID / name.

Changing them on a live shop keeps the shop live, resets her confirmation (as before) and keeps the old, confirmed
values on every customer-facing page (shop, order thank-you, UPI link) until she confirms the new ones. My shops
says what she still has to confirm. A practice shop shows changes at once (nobody else sees it).
"""

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app.models import AuditEvent
from tests.conftest import publish, ready_for_real, sign_in
from tests.test_m3_launch import approve, meera, plan
from tests.test_s9_phase1 import HOST, ORDER

OLD_UPI, NEW_UPI = "meera.cakes@okaxis", "someone.else@ybl"
OLD_WA_DIGITS, NEW_WA = "9876543210", "91234 56789"


def live_shop(client, engine) -> dict:
    sign_in(client, "meera@example.org")
    biz = meera(client)
    ready_for_real(client, biz["id"])
    assert approve(client, plan(client, biz))["status"] == "done"
    publish(engine, biz["id"])
    return client.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}").json()


def edit(client, biz: dict, **changes) -> dict:
    cur = client.get(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}").json()
    r = client.put(f"/api/businesses/{biz['id']}", json={"profile": {**cur["profile"], **changes}, "subdomain": cur["subdomain"]})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.json()


def shop(client) -> str:
    r = client.get("/", headers=HOST)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    return r.text


def order_page(client) -> str:
    r = client.post("/order", data=ORDER, headers=HOST)
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    return r.text


def wa(html: str, number: str) -> bool:
    return f"wa.me/91{number}" in html


def test_changed_upi_stays_old_for_customers_until_she_confirms(client, engine):
    biz = live_shop(client, engine)
    assert OLD_UPI not in shop(client)  # S20: the shop page never carries the UPI ID
    edit(client, biz, payment_terms="upfront")  # so the thank-you page carries a UPI link for the full amount
    out = edit(client, biz, upi_id=NEW_UPI, upi_display_name="Someone Else")

# PROGRESS — master status

Claude Code reads this at the start of every session and updates it at the end. Keep it short and current; history goes in `BUILD_LOG.md`.

## Current milestone

**Session 19D (Nov 19, Opus, laptop): View shop, edit a live shop, New badge, safe live edits.** My shops: View shop (live
real shops, own address in a new tab, address shown) or Preview (practice/draft), Edit shop. A live shop's owner can edit and
add items; items can show "New" for 15 days. Customers never see an unconfirmed WhatsApp/UPI, and changed words on a live shop
pass the policy check first (held edits wait for the team; the shop stays live). 19C deploy confirmed. **Next: demo video,
submission.**

Decisions (S19D): `live_url` is set for a real live shop also when paused / held / on a break (its own page says so); the
Report keeps its existing "Open my shop" (hidden while a check runs, as before). Removing a WhatsApp/UPI value takes effect at
once (nothing to confirm). New badge: `new_until` = day marked + 15 (IST), shown while today <= new_until, server never stores
more than 15 days ahead; items added after launch are New by default; the badge uses the theme's accent/accent-ink pair (the
button pair, AA in every look). Only a change to the words the policy check reads (name, tagline, about, selling point, item
names/descriptions) re-runs it; prices, hours, photos, the badge, theme don't. While an edit is held she keeps editing her own
copy; any later save that still carries the held words waits too; taking them out publishes. A real server on saved Claude
answers holds every word edit (as launches). The team sees the held edit through "See the edit" (the owner's Review). The
local e2e stack allows 1000 live shops (`docker-compose.local.yml`; production keeps 40). Hero trace (new script, different
settings from 19C, so not comparable): live, full Chrome headless, 1440: 60-68 fps, idle 3.6%, CLS 0.027; 390 px x4 (DPR 3,
scrolling through the dark panel): 16-18 fps, idle 23-28%, CLS 0.0006.

**Session 19C (Nov 19, Opus, laptop): landing hero performance.** The 19A hero kept the main thread busy every frame (idle
37-47% desktop / 98% on a 4x-throttled phone; scroll 20 fps desktop, 9 fps phone). Measured with CDP traces, fixed the causes,
same look on desktop (frozen-frame pixel diff < 0.06%). Landing files only. Numbers, method and screenshots:
`docs/screenshots/hero-perf/` and BUILD_LOG 19C. **Next: demo video, submission.**

Decisions (S19C): phones / low-power devices (< 900 px wide, <= 4 CPU cores, or Save-Data) get a lighter hero: the light-lines
are drawn still (no drift, no glowing dots) and the stack does not spread apart on scroll; everything else (intro, breathing
stack, ring ball, card scale/dim/corners on scroll) is unchanged. All hero loops pause while the hero is off screen or fully
covered by the dark panel. Found, not fixed (out of scope): shop subdomains answer `/favicon.ico` with 404, which fails
`l-s16-themes` (6 tests) when e2e runs on full Google Chrome (`LW_CHROME`); the bundled headless browser never asks for it.

**Session 19B (Nov 19, Opus, laptop): test emails only when she asks, clearly marked TEST; everything re-checked and deployed.**
Launch / "Run checks now" / "Describe the problem" send the test order to the shop's order address; monitoring sends it to
LaunchWitness's own check mailbox (hello@), labelled as such, with no "Yes, I got it" link. Every test email starts
`TEST, not a real order:` with a grey banner and no customer links; real order emails unchanged. 19A (landing motion) was
already merged by the owner and deployed. VPS on the final `main`. **Next: demo video, submission.**

## 9d. Where she sells, how she is paid (S15)

A shop says where it sells (`selling_mode`: pickup, local delivery, ships across India; pickup can combine with one of the others), shows only city + locality (never a home address; the exact pickup address is shared by the seller on WhatsApp), and takes orders by these rules, all enforced on the server: customer picks pickup or delivery; delivery needs an address + 6-digit PIN, and for local delivery the PIN or a locality in the address must be one she serves (else "<shop> delivers only in <areas>. You could choose pickup instead."); the wanted-by date respects minimum notice, days off and an optional orders-per-day limit; optional time slots; totals (items + delivery/shipping fee) come from the menu only. Payment terms: full upfront, an advance of 10-90%, or on delivery/pickup (+ accepts cash); the UPI link/QR after ordering carries the exact amount and the order ref. Cancellation preset or one plain line; food marks (veg / contains egg / non-veg, always with a word) and allergens; a "taking a break" switch with optional return date refuses orders on the server. The customer's address is visible only to the owner (Orders page, order email), never in audit, evidence, the shared report or the public pages, and is deleted with the shop. The go-live checklist requires a valid mode with its fields; drafts and practice are never blocked. The checker's test order uses pickup (or a test address inside her area) and ignores date rules and the break.

## 10. Budget

**GoDaddy:** VPS is added to the cart at $0 by organizers. ~$25 in-store credit covers domain + email. Buy on godaddy.com only after organizers confirm credit; use the CLI to explore and manage.

| Item | Paid by | Expected cost | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 vCPU / 8 GB Docker VPS | Organizers ($0 in cart) | $0 | Check out after confirmation |
| App domain | Credit | Cart price; compare with `gddy` | Buy first (unlocks DNS) |
| Titan Pro Light, 1-month term, 1 mailbox | Credit | ~$2–5 | Buy after domain; create hello@ with `gddy` |
| Meera's demo domain | Credit, if room | Cart price | One full launch for the recording |
| Meera's own mailbox | Credit, if room | Another Pro Light month | Likely skip; test orders go to app mailbox (say so) |

If money runs out: skip Meera's domain; full launch on a subdomain; show purchase in dry-run. SMTP tip: if login fails use `smtpout.secureserver.net` with the full address as username.

**Claude: $100, API only, for the product.** None of it for Claude Code.
- ~3 small calls per launch (cents).
- Strong model only for Reader; cheap for Namer + Doctor.
- Dev: saved fixtures, not live calls, for UI work.
- Live link: per-visitor limit, max-token cap per call, daily spend cap.
- Check spend in the Claude console daily.

content.content:
## 13. Judge Q&A

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Doesn't GoDaddy already have AI for this? | GoDaddy's AI helps people get online. LaunchWitness proves it works (a real order in her inbox) and fixes what doesn't, before customers notice. |
| Who owns the domain? | Demo: my account. Real product: her own GoDaddy account, so she owns everything. |
| What can break after launch? | Not much in a setup we control. Real risks: renewal failing, someone changing settings while connecting another tool. Monitoring is insurance. |
| If her email breaks, how do you alert her? | Personal email, not the business inbox. |
| What if she changes a setting on purpose? | Not undone silently; it asks "Was this you?" first (full monitoring). Auto-fix only when a check fails. |
| What if your server goes down? | Checks stop too. Next step: outside uptime pinger. |
| Why trust AI with money and DNS? | It can't act alone: approval, preview, backup/undo, fixed fixes, spend caps in code. |
| Where does Claude matter? | Messy price list/photo → clean profile + copy; brand-fit names; plain-words diagnosis. Code acts. |
| Why VPS not GoDaddy Hosting? | Docker VPS option runs FastAPI + many seller sites with automatic HTTPS from one box. |
| Confirm delivery for real sellers? | "Yes, I got it" link in the test email; no mailbox password [REDACTED] |
| Was the demo failure real? | Staged so it shows reliably; detection and fix are real code. |
| Cost per seller? | A few Claude calls (cents) + domain + mailbox she'd buy anyway. |
| How does she get paid? | Each order shows "Pay ₹X via UPI": a prefilled UPI link on phones and a QR on laptops, with the order ID as the note. Money goes straight from the customer's UPI app to hers; it never passes through us. She marks the order Paid after checking her UPI app. Card payments ("Connect Razorpay") come later, after the seller's KYC. |
| How does the customer know what's happening? | A status page per order (unguessable ID, first name + items only), plus a ready-typed WhatsApp message the seller sends with one tap. No SMS, no WhatsApp Business API. |
| What if she never opens her business inbox? | New orders also go to her personal email, and the customer can send the order to her WhatsApp from the thank-you screen. |
| Can a scammer launch a fake shop? | The owner's email is verified before a real launch, a policy check can hold a shop for review, every shop has "Report this shop", and the team can pause it. |
| Can a salon or tutor use it? | Not yet: v1 is for sellers who take orders. The Reader says so plainly instead of building a half-working shop. |
| Who pays renewal next year? | The seller, to GoDaddy, on her own account. We warn her at 30 / 7 / 1 days. |
| Won't sellers get annoyed by test emails? | A seller gets a test only when she launches or asks for a check, and it's clearly marked TEST. Our daily checks send their test order to LaunchWitness's own mailbox. |

---

## 14. Risks and fallbacks

| Risk | Check by | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Credits not yet received | Office hours Nov 14 | Build locally against OTE + fakes |
| Domain + Pro Light cost more than credit | Cart, Nov 15 | Cheaper TLD; skip Meera's domain + mailbox |
| Production Availability/DNS API blocked | Nov 15 after app domain | `gddy`, OTE or RDAP; app domain unlocks DNS |
| Mailbox creation fails via CLI/API | Nov 15 | Create in dashboard; engine still sets settings + checks delivery |
| Settings/cert slow on camera | Nov 18 rehearsal | Query authoritative NS; record the full launch |
| Claude spend creeps up | Daily | Fixtures in dev, caps on live link |
| Others build the same launch flow | — | Lead with proof + fix |
| Scope creep | Daily | No stretch before core runs end to end |
| Live demo fails at Dec 11 finale | Dec 11 | Play recording, then Q&A on live app |

+## Part A audit: where the seller's UPI ID / name / QR appeared before
+| Shop page `#pay` tile (`seller.html`, `render.py` `upi`/`upi_qr`) | ID, name, QR, `upi://` link on every public view | **removed** (also not in the owner's preview) |
+| "How to pay" tile | plain words | plain words only; says the UPI details come after ordering |
+| Thank-you page (POST `/order`) | QR + link with exact amount | unchanged, **plus** the "I've paid" form; test orders get none of it |
+| Status page | did not exist | new `GET /order/<48-char token>` on the shop host (same page, `no-store`, `noindex`) |
+| Owner preview | tile with ID | no tile; the owner's ₹1 test is the `/golive` API (`upi_test`), shown on her go-live screen only |
+| Demo shops (`/demo/*`) | no UPI (stripped) | same + a line "you'll see the UPI details after ordering" |
+| `live_contact.public_profile` | last confirmed UPI to customers | unchanged; still the profile the thank-you/status page uses |
+| Tests | asserted the ID on the shop page | now assert it is absent; present on thank-you/status |
+| `payment_terms` paths | upfront / advance / on_delivery | unchanged (see decision 3) |
+- Shop host: `GET /order/<token>`, `POST /order/<token>/paid` (multipart, no JS; 303 back to the status page).

+- UTR: exactly 12 ASCII digits, spaces and dashes accepted. Screenshot: `photos.clean_image` (new shared gate extracted from the photo pipeline): 4 MB cap, content sniff JPEG/PNG/WebP, 40 MP cap, EXIF-upright, re-encoded from pixels as one 900 px WebP.
+- Rate limits: 6 submits per order, 10 per visitor per hour. A second submit replaces the first (audited as "replaced an earlier claim"); the owner is emailed once.

+- Owner: Orders page "Customer says paid · UTR 1234 5678 9012 · View screenshot" (`GET /api/businesses/{id}/orders/{oid}/payment-screenshot`: owner gate, app host only, `private, no-store`, sandboxed CSP). Wording is "says paid" everywhere; only her status button makes it Paid.
+- Email through the outbox (`kind=payment_claim`, body emptied once sent, no `order_id` so the order's own email status is untouched).

+- Privacy: UTR/screenshot never in audit rows (only "customer says paid[, with a screenshot]"), evidence, report, logs, public pages. Deleted with the order/shop/account (`_purge_extra`) and 30 days after the order is Done/Cancelled (`purge_old`, daily job + once at start-up). Shop privacy page updated.

+- `app/sites/motifs.py`: 18 motifs (3 per theme) and 3 arrangements (scatter / corner / band), seeded from the shop name (sha256), drawn as SVG from numbers only. `Profile.motif` / `Profile.art` (keys, validated per theme, "" = chosen by code). `PUT /api/businesses/{id}/signature` (owner, audited `signature_changed`); a theme change drops a foreign motif. Look picker shows live thumbnails.

+- `templates/js/fx.js` (one more fixed, hash-allowed script) + `templates/css/fx.css`: add-to-basket fly + bump, quick-view `<dialog>` sheet (stepper drives the real quantity box), scroll-spy sticky category bar, reveal on scroll, motif drift (paused off screen), New-badge shimmer once. Progressive: JS off = the page and form exactly as before; `prefers-reduced-motion` = no movement.
+1. **Status page** (`/order/<token>`) was needed (none existed). Token: `secrets.token_urlsafe(24)`, separate from the client's form token; test orders have none.
+2. **Claim is only ever a claim.** A claim can be sent while the order is New/Confirmed/Paid, not after Done/Cancelled; only when there was something to pay now.

+3. **Smaller safe version for "pay on delivery":** S15 says that order asks for nothing now and shows no `upi://` link. Before S20 those customers could still read the UPI ID on the shop page; now they can't, so the shop page says "ask the shop on WhatsApp for its UPI details". No new payment path was invented.

+4. **Motif opacity .08** (the CSS value; an earlier draft of this note said .09). The AA test (every theme × accent × background × ink/ink2/muted, worst-case motif pixel) fails at the first guess (.17) and at .12; .08 with shapes at ≤80% passes. Subtle by design.
+5. UTR regex uses `[0-9]`, not `\d` (a test found `\d` accepts Arabic-Indic digits).
+6. Per-visitor claim limit uses the claim row's `updated_at`, not a new table.
+7. The screenshot is stored as one 900 px WebP in the DB (not two widths).
+8. **Gifts "build your box" not built** (explicitly optional, "only if time allows").
+9. The recording is a filmstrip PNG (`add-to-basket-and-quick-view-filmstrip.png`): this sandbox has no working video encoder.

+10. Existing tests that encoded the old behaviour were changed on purpose: UPI absent from the shop page (`test_m2_site`, `test_s8_shop`, `test_s14_themes`, `test_s19d_live_contact`), two fixed scripts instead of one (`test_s10_xss`, `test_s14_themes`), the access matrix skips the 200-read of the screenshot route (it 404s until a claim has one; covered in `test_s20_payments`).

"""Team tool (S19B): run one round of checks for a shop from the command line, inside the app container, through the
same code the app uses. Prints results, the test email's SUBJECT only (never addresses, bodies or secrets), the
shared-report count and whether the proof chain is intact. Every run is audited (actor "admin (cli)").

    docker compose ... exec -T app python /app/scripts/admin_check_shop.py <subdomain> manual|daily

manual = what "Run checks now" does (test email to the shop's order address, with "Yes, I got it").
daily  = one daily monitoring round (test email to LaunchWitness's check mailbox), plus the later inbox passes.
"""

import json
import sys
import time

from sqlmodel import Session, select

from app import audit, chain, proof
from app.agents.launch_check import latest_launched_plan, run_checks
from app.config import get_settings
from app.db import get_engine
from app.integrations import for_business, get_integrations, get_practice_integrations
from app.models import Business, CheckResult, CheckRun, Order, Outbox, TestTicket
from app.routers.businesses import get_claude
from app.routers.report import run_out
from app.sites.orders import TEST_BANNER


def since_of(t: TestTicket):
    from datetime import UTC, timedelta

    at = t.created_at if t.created_at.tzinfo else t.created_at.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
    return at - timedelta(minutes=2)


def main(subdomain: str, kind: str) -> int:
    settings, engine = get_settings(), get_engine()
    server, practice = get_integrations(), get_practice_integrations()
    integ_for = lambda b: for_business(b, server, practice)  # noqa: E731
    claude = get_claude(settings)
    with Session(engine) as s:
        b = s.exec(select(Business).where(Business.subdomain == subdomain)).first()
        if b is None:
            print("no such shop")
            return 2
        plan = latest_launched_plan(s, b.id)
        audit.record(s, actor="admin (cli)", action="run_checks_now" if kind == "manual" else "monitor_daily_now",
                     target=plan.site_host, result="ok", business_id=b.id, detail="scripts/admin_check_shop.py")
        bid, plan_id = b.id, plan.id
    if kind == "manual":
        summary = run_checks(engine, settings, integ_for(b), claude, plan_id, trigger="manual")
        run_id = summary.run_id
    else:
        from app.monitor.scheduler import Monitor

        mon = Monitor(engine, settings, integ_for, claude)
        mon.check_business(bid, "daily")
        jobs = [j for j in mon.scheduler.get_jobs() if j.id.startswith("inbox-")]
        for job in jobs:  # the later inbox passes the running scheduler would do, one minute apart
            _b, run_id, item, n = job.args
            while True:
